questions.question: According to the National Commission for Women data released in January 2025, which Indian state reported the highest number of complaints of domestic violence in 2024?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Uttar Pradesh**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **National Commission for Women (NCW)** released its annual statistical report in **January 2025**, highlighting that **Uttar Pradesh** continues to record the highest number of complaints regarding crimes against women, including **domestic violence**.
 
• According to the data for the year **2024**, the **NCW** received a total of **24,535 complaints** from across the country, out of which **Uttar Pradesh** alone accounted for nearly **50.6%** of the total grievances.
 
• Of the total complaints originating from **Uttar Pradesh**, a significant volume (approximately **12,410 cases**) was related to the **"Right to Dignity"** and **domestic violence**, maintaining the state's position at the top of the list for the consecutive year.
 
• Following **Uttar Pradesh**, the **National Capital Territory of Delhi** recorded the second-highest number of complaints with **2,330**, while **Maharashtra** stood third with **1,326** complaints registered in **2024**.
 
• The data indicates that the **"Right to Dignity"** category, which includes harassment other than domestic violence, saw the highest number of overall filings, followed closely by specific complaints of **domestic abuse** and **dowry harassment**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Uttar Pradesh.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **National Commission for Women (NCW):**
 
 
• The **NCW** is a **statutory body** of the **Government of India**, established on **31 January 1992**.
 
• It was formed under the **National Commission for Women Act, 1990**, with the mandate to review constitutional and legal safeguards for women and recommend remedial legislative measures.
 
• The **NCW** consists of a **Chairperson**, five **members**, and a **Member-Secretary**, all nominated by the **Central Government**.
 
• As of **January 2025**, the **Chairperson** of the commission is **Vijaya Rahatkar**, who took charge in **October 2024**, succeeding **Rekha Sharma**.
 
 
 
• **Legislative Framework for Protection:**
 
 
• The **Protection of Women from Domestic Violence Act, 2005 (PWDVA)** is a key civil law that provides protection and support to women facing abuse within a domestic relationship.
 
• Criminal provisions such as **Section 498A** of the **Indian Penal Code (IPC)** (now integrated into the **Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita**) deal specifically with cruelty by the husband or his relatives.
 
• The **NCW** facilitates the registration of these complaints and monitors the action taken by the respective **state police departments**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Reporting Mechanisms:**
 
 
• The **NCW** launched a **24/7 Helpline Number (7827170170)** to provide online support to women in distress, which has seen a surge in usage in states like **Uttar Pradesh** and **Delhi**.
 
• The high volume of complaints in **Uttar Pradesh** is often attributed to the state's massive **population** (approx **240 million**) and intensified awareness campaigns like **"Mission Shakti"** launched by the state government.
 
 
 
• **Nature of Complaints in 2024:**
 
 
• Nationwide, **8,115** complaints were classified under **"Right to Dignity"**, while **6,150** were specifically related to **domestic violence**.
 
• Complaints regarding **molestation** stood at **1,820**, and cases of **rape or attempt to rape** accounted for **1,200** filings in the **2024** calendar year.
 
• The **NCW** also possesses **suo motu** powers to take cognizance of incidents reported in the media and initiate independent investigations.
 
 
</ul

questions.question: Which Gujarati children’s poet won the Bal Sahitya Puraskar for Tinchak in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kirtida Brahmbhatt**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kirtida Brahmbhatt**, a noted **Gujarati** author and poet, was selected for the prestigious **Sahitya Akademi Bal Sahitya Puraskar**.
 
• The award was conferred for her outstanding **poetry collection** titled **Tinchak**, which is specifically written for children.
 
• The announcement of the winners for the **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** usually occurs in **June**, as part of the **Sahitya Akademi's** annual recognition of excellence in children's literature.
 
• For the **Gujarati** language category, the selection was made based on the recommendations of a **three-member jury** that evaluates the literary merit and creative contribution of works published in the preceding years.
 
• This recognition highlights **Kirtida Brahmbhatt's** significant role in enriching **Gujarati children's literature** and fostering a love for poetry among young readers.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Sahitya Akademi Bal Sahitya Puraskar**:
 
 
• This award was instituted in the **year 2010** to promote and recognize high-quality literature written for children.
 
• It covers **24 Indian languages**, including those listed in the **Eighth Schedule** of the **Indian Constitution**, as well as **English** and **Rajasthani**.
 
• The award consists of a **copper plaque** and a cash prize of **Rs. 50,000**.
 
 
 
• **Other Notable Recipients (2024 Context)**:
 
 
• **Nandini Purandare**: Won the award in the **English** category for her biography titled **'Mountain Fairies: The Inspiring Life of Tenzing Norgay'**.
 
• **Akhil P Dharmajan**: Recognized in the **Malayalam** category for his novel **'Ramante Kayyum Thozuthu Pookkalum'**.
 
• **Parvati Tirkey**: While mentioned in literary awards circles, she is the recipient of the **Sahitya Akademi Yuva Puraskar** for **Santali** poetry, rather than the Bal Sahitya Puraskar.
 
 
 
• **Sahitya Akademi**:
 
 
• Founded on **12 March 1954**, it is **India's National Academy of Letters**.
 
• It functions as an autonomous organization under the **Ministry of Culture**, Government of India, to promote literary dialogue and publication across various regional languages.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** is one of the twin honors announced mid-year, the other being the **Yuva Puraskar**, which is awarded to young authors under the **age of 35**.
 
• The selection criteria for the **Bal Sahitya Puraskar** require that the author must be an **Indian national** and the work must be an original contribution to the genre of children's books.
 
• The **Sahitya Akademi** also publishes translated versions of award-winning books to ensure that children across **India** can enjoy the diverse literary heritage of different states.
</ul

questions.question: At COP30 (November 2025), the “Baku–Belem Roadmap” aimed to scale climate finance to what annual level by 2035?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**US$1.3 trillion**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Baku–Belem Roadmap** was established to ensure a seamless transition and continuity between the **COP29** presidency in **Azerbaijan** and the **COP30** presidency in **Brazil**.
 
• A primary objective of this roadmap is to finalize and scale the **New Collective Quantified Goal (NCQG)**, which is the successor to the previous **US$100 billion** annual climate finance target.
 
• At the conclusion of the negotiations leading toward **COP30** in **November 2025**, the global community aimed to set a target for climate finance to reach an annual level of **US$1.3 trillion** by the year **2035**.
 
• This **US$1.3 trillion** figure represents the total "global goal" for climate finance intended for **developing nations** to support their **mitigation** and **adaptation** efforts. ***Hence, the target of US$1.3 trillion is the correct annual level.***
 
• The roadmap emphasizes the "Mission 1.5°C" initiative, which focuses on keeping the global temperature rise within the limits set by the **Paris Agreement** through enhanced **Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **The COP Presidencies Troika:**
 
 
• The **Troika** is a collaborative partnership consisting of three consecutive presidencies: **COP28 (UAE)**, **COP29 (Azerbaijan)**, and **COP30 (Brazil)**.
 
• Its purpose is to maintain momentum in international climate negotiations and provide a clear pathway toward the **Belem** summit in **2025**.
 
 
 
• **Structure of the Finance Goal:**
 
 
• While the overarching goal is **US$1.3 trillion** annually by **2035**, a specific "core" mobilization goal of **US$300 billion** per year was designated for **developed countries** to lead by **2035**.
 
• This includes funds from **public**, **private**, **bilateral**, and **multilateral** sources, including **Multilateral Development Banks (MDBs)**.
 
 
 
• **Significance of COP30:**
 
 
• **COP30**, scheduled for **November 2025** in **Belem, Brazil**, is considered a landmark event as it marks the **10th anniversary** of the **Paris Agreement**.
 
• It is the deadline for countries to submit their updated and more ambitious **NDCs** for the **2030-2035** period.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Climate Justice and Equity:** Many **developing nations** and groups like the **G77 + China** argued that the **US$1.3 trillion** should primarily come from **public grants** rather than loans to avoid increasing the debt burden on vulnerable economies.
 
• **Historical Context:** The **US$100 billion** goal was originally set at **COP15** in **Copenhagen** in **2009**, but developed nations faced criticism for delays in meeting this target, which was finally achieved only in **2022**.
 
• **NCQG Purpose:** The **New Collective Quantified Goal** is designed to reflect the evolving financial needs of **Global South** countries to combat **climate change** impacts like **sea-level rise**, **extreme weather**, and **biodiversity loss**.

questions.question: Which cyclonic storm in November 2025 caused widespread flooding and prompted disaster relief responses in South India and Sri Lanka?
questions.solution:
p>The correct answer is __**Cyclone Ditwah**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Ditwah** is identified as the cyclonic storm that occurred in **November 2025**, leading to intense precipitation and severe **flooding** across **South India** and **Sri Lanka**.
 
• The storm originated in the **Bay of Bengal** as a low-pressure system and rapidly intensified into a **Very Severe Cyclonic Storm** with wind speeds ranging between **120 and 150 km/h**.
 
• It made landfall near the coastal regions of **Tamil Nadu** and the northern provinces of **Sri Lanka**, causing significant damage to infrastructure, power grids, and agricultural land.
 
• The **National Disaster Response Force (NDRF)** in **India** and the **Disaster Management Centre (DMC)** in **Sri Lanka** spearheaded the **disaster relief** efforts, evacuating over **200,000 people** to relief camps.
 
• Urban areas such as **Chennai** and **Colombo** experienced unprecedented **waterlogging**, which prompted the suspension of railway and aviation services for several days.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Cyclone Tauktae**:
 
 
• This was a powerful **Extremely Severe Cyclonic Storm** that developed in the **Arabian Sea** in **May 2021**.
 
• It primarily affected the **Western coast of India**, including the states of **Gujarat**, **Maharashtra**, **Goa**, and **Karnataka**.
 
• It was the strongest cyclone to strike **Gujarat** since the **1998** Kandla cyclone, leading to substantial industrial disruptions.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone Amphan**:
 
 
• Occurring in **May 2020**, **Amphan** was the first **Super Cyclonic Storm** to form in the **Bay of Bengal** since **1999**.
 
• It caused catastrophic destruction in **West Bengal** and **Bangladesh**, with damages estimated at over **$13 billion USD**.
 
• The storm was characterized by a massive **storm surge** that inundated the **Sundarbans** delta.
 
 
 
• **Cyclone Yaas**:
 
 
• This **Very Severe Cyclonic Storm** formed in the **Bay of Bengal** in **May 2021**, shortly after Tauktae.
 
• It made landfall in the **Balasore district** of **Odisha**, causing widespread damage to kucha houses and saline water flooding in coastal villages.
 
• The storm's impact was felt as far as **West Bengal** and **Jharkhand**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Naming of Cyclones**: Tropical cyclones in the **North Indian Ocean** are named by the **WMO/ESCAP** Panel on Tropical Cyclones, which consists of **13 member countries** including **India**, **Sri Lanka**, and **Thailand**.
 
• **Role of IMD**: The **India Meteorological Department (IMD)** serves as the **Regional Specialized Meteorological Centre (RSMC)** for providing tropical cyclone advisories to the region.
 
• **Classification**: Cyclones are categorized based on their **Maximum Sustained Surface Wind Speed (MSW)**. A "Severe Cyclonic Storm" typically features wind speeds of **89–117 km/h** (48–63 knots).
 
• **Mitigation Tools**: Modern technologies such as **Doppler Weather Radars (DWR)** and **Ocean-buoys** help in the early detection and tracking of these systems to minimize the loss of **human life** and **livestock**.

questions.question: Manu Bhaker, who received the Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award in 2025, is primarily known for her achievements in which sport?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Shooting**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Manu Bhaker** is a renowned Indian **sport shooter** who has represented the country in various international platforms, specializing in the **10m Air Pistol** and **25m Pistol** events.
 
• She achieved monumental success at the **2024 Paris Olympics**, where she won **two bronze medals**. This feat made her the **first Indian athlete** since Independence to win two medals in a single edition of the **Olympic Games**.
 
• One of her medals was won in the **Women's 10m Air Pistol** event, and the second was a **Mixed Team 10m Air Pistol** bronze, which she won alongside partner **Sarabjot Singh**.
 
• In recognition of her extraordinary contribution to Indian sports and her historic performance at the Olympics, she was conferred with the **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award** in **2025**.
 
• Hailing from **Goria village** in the **Jhajjar district** of **Haryana**, she started her shooting career at a very young age and quickly rose to prominence by winning gold at the **2018 Commonwealth Games** at just **16 years old**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Shooting.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• This is the **highest sporting honor** in India, awarded annually by the **Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports**.
 
• The award was formerly known as the **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** but was renamed in **August 2021** in honor of the legendary hockey player **Major Dhyan Chand**.
 
• The first recipient of this prestigious award was the Chess Grandmaster **Viswanathan Anand** in the year **1991-92**.
 
 
 
• **Other Sports mentioned in the options:**
 
 
• **Badminton:** India has a strong presence in this sport with athletes like **P.V. Sindhu**, who is a two-time Olympic medalist, and **Saina Nehwal**.
 
• **Hockey:** Often regarded as India's national game in spirit, the **Indian Men’s Hockey Team** has won multiple Olympic medals, including a bronze at both **Tokyo 2020** and **Paris 2024**.
 
• **Para-Athletics:** This refers to sports for athletes with disabilities. India has seen a surge in performance here, with stars like **Sumit Antil** (Javelin Throw) winning gold medals at the **Paralympic Games**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Early Achievements:** **Manu Bhaker** became the youngest Indian to win a gold medal at the **ISSF World Cup** in **2018**, held in **Guadalajara, Mexico**.
 
• **Arjuna Award:** Before receiving the Khel Ratna, she was honored with the **Arjuna Award** in **2020** for her consistent performance in international shooting competitions.
 
• **Olympic History:** Prior to **Paris 2024**, India’s shooting medals at the Olympics were won by **Abhinav Bindra** (Gold, 2008), **Rajyavardhan Singh Rathore** (Silver, 2004), **Vijay Kumar** (Silver, 2012), and **Gagan Narang** (Bronze, 2012). Manu Bhaker ended a **12-year medal drought** for Indian shooting in **2024**.
 
• **Academic Background:** Apart from her sporting career, she pursued a degree in **Political Science** from **Lady Shri Ram College**, Delhi University, balancing rigorous training with education.

questions.question: According to the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), May 2025, what was India’s overall unemployment rate reported by the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI)?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5.6%**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MOSPI)** released the findings of the **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS)** for the quarter ending **May 2025**.
 
• According to the official data, **India’s overall unemployment rate** was reported at **5.6%**. This figure represents the percentage of the labor force that is unemployed and actively seeking employment.
 
• The **PLFS** is a primary source of high-frequency labor market data in India, helping policymakers understand the dynamics of employment across **urban** and **rural** sectors.
 
• The survey focuses on key indicators such as the **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR)** and the **Worker Population Ratio (WPR)** to provide a holistic view of the economy.
 
• For the period of **May 2025**, the data highlights the stabilization of the job market compared to previous fiscal quarters, reflecting the impact of various economic policies and industrial growth.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS):**
 
 
• Launched in **April 2017** by the **National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)**, the **PLFS** was designed to provide more frequent labor force statistics.
 
• It has two main objectives: to estimate key employment indicators in the **Current Weekly Status (CWS)** every three months for **urban areas**, and to provide annual estimates in both **Usual Status** and **CWS** for both **rural** and **urban** areas.
 
 
 
• **Key Terminology:**
 
 
• **Unemployment Rate (UR):** It is defined as the percentage of persons unemployed among the persons in the **labour force**.
 
• **Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR):** This is defined as the percentage of persons in the **labour force** (i.e., working or seeking or available for work) in the total population.
 
• **Worker Population Ratio (WPR):** This is defined as the percentage of employed persons in the total population.
 
 
 
• **Role of MOSPI:**
 
 
• The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation** is the nodal agency for the planned and organized development of the statistical system in **India**.
 
• It consists of two wings: the **Statistics Wing** (consisting of the **NSO**) and the **Programme Implementation Wing**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Survey Methodology:** The **PLFS** utilizes a **rotational panel sampling** design in **urban areas** to measure short-term changes in the labor market every **quarter**.
 
• **Activity Status:** The survey classifies individuals based on their activity during a specific reference period. **Usual Status** considers a reference period of **365 days**, while **Current Weekly Status (CWS)** considers a reference period of the last **7 days**.
 
• **Age Criteria:** While the **PLFS** collects data for all ages, the key indicators for policy analysis are typically highlighted for the age group of **15 years and above**.
 
• **Data Utility:** The reported **5.6%** unemployment rate is used by the **Government of India** and international organizations like the **ILO** to monitor **Sustainable Development Goals (SDG)** related to decent work and economic growth.
</ul

questions.question: Rajasthan’s first Namo Biodiversity Park, inaugurated in October 2025, is located in which district?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Alwar District**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The state of **Rajasthan** achieved a new milestone in environmental conservation with the inauguration of its first **Namo Biodiversity Park** in **October 2025**.
 
• This prestigious project is located in the **Alwar District**, a region known for its rich ecological heritage and proximity to the **Aravalli Range**.
 
• The park has been developed to serve as a **natural habitat** for various **indigenous species** of flora and fauna, ensuring the preservation of the local ecosystem.
 
• The **Namo Biodiversity Park** is designed to promote **eco-tourism** and provide a dedicated space for **environmental research** and **nature education** for students and researchers.
 
• The establishment of this park in **Alwar** highlights the **Government of Rajasthan's** commitment to increasing green cover and mitigating the effects of **climate change** in the semi-arid regions of the state.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Alwar District:**
 
 
• **Alwar** is often referred to as the **Gateway to Rajasthan** and is a significant part of the **National Capital Region (NCR)**.
 
• It is home to the famous **Sariska Tiger Reserve**, which was the first reserve in the world to successfully relocate tigers.
 
• The district features diverse topography, including the **Aravalli Hills**, which play a crucial role in preventing the expansion of the **Thar Desert**.
 
 
 
• **Biodiversity Parks in India:**
 
 
• A **Biodiversity Park** is a unique landscape of **community-based ecosystems** that helps in the restoration of **degraded land** and provides **ecosystem services** such as **carbon sequestration** and **groundwater recharge**.
 
• These parks act as **lungs** for urban and semi-urban areas, significantly improving **air quality** and providing a refuge for **migratory birds** and **pollinators**.
 
 
 
• **Other Ecological Initiatives in Rajasthan:**
 
 
• **Jaipur**: Known for the **Kishan Bagh Sand Dune Park** and the **Jhalana Leopard Reserve**, which are key sites for ecological restoration.
 
• **Udaipur**: Famous for its **Sajjangarh Biological Park** and numerous lakes that support diverse **aquatic biodiversity**.
 
• **Kota**: Home to the **Mukundra Hills Tiger Reserve** and various riverine ecosystems along the **Chambal River**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

• Key features of the park include **herbal gardens**, **butterfly zones**, and **walking trails** designed to minimize human impact on the core **conservation zones**.
 
• The **October 2025** inauguration marks a strategic move to utilize the **post-monsoon season**, which is the most favorable time for the growth of new plantations and the arrival of **winter migratory birds** in the **Alwar** region.
 
• Local **Panchayati Raj Institutions** and the **State Forest Department** are the primary bodies responsible for the long-term maintenance and protection of this **biodiversity hotspot**.

questions.question: Which All‑India Financial Institution coordinates financing of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSME) according to the Dept of Financial Services Annual Report 2024‑25 published in March 2025?

options.text: Small Industrial Development Bank of India (SIDBI)
National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD)
National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID)

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Small Industrial Development Bank of India (SIDBI)**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Small Industrial Development Bank of India (SIDBI)** is the principal financial institution in India for the **promotion, financing, and development** of the **Micro, Small, and Medium Enterprises (MSME)** sector.
 
• According to the **Department of Financial Services (DFS) Annual Report 2024-25**, published in **March 2025**, **SIDBI** continues to serve as the apex body for coordinating the functions of institutions engaged in similar activities.
 
• **SIDBI** was established on **April 2, 1990**, under an **Act of the Indian Parliament**. It originally operated as a wholly-owned subsidiary of the **Industrial Development Bank of India (IDBI)**, but is currently an independent **All-India Financial Institution (AIFI)**.
 
• The headquarters of **SIDBI** is located in **Lucknow**, **Uttar Pradesh**. Its primary objective is to facilitate and strengthen credit flow to **MSMEs** and address both financial and developmental gaps in the **MSME ecosystem**.
 
• It serves as the nodal agency for several government schemes, including the **Credit Linked Capital Subsidy Scheme (CLCSS)** and the **PM Vishwakarma scheme**, ensuring financial inclusion for small-scale entrepreneurs. ***Hence, the correct answer is Small Industrial Development Bank of India (SIDBI).***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Export-Import Bank of India (Exim Bank):**
 
 
• Established in **1982** under the **Export-Import Bank of India Act, 1981**, it is headquartered in **Mumbai**.
 
• Its primary function is to provide financial assistance to **exporters and importers** and function as the principal financial institution for coordinating the working of institutions engaged in financing **export and import of goods and services**.
 
 
 
• **National Bank for Agriculture and Rural Development (NABARD):**
 
 
• Established on **July 12, 1982**, based on the recommendations of the **B. Sivaraman Committee**.
 
• Headquartered in **Mumbai**, it is the apex regulatory body for the overall regulation and licensing of **regional rural banks** and **apex cooperative banks** in India. It focuses on **rural prosperity** and **agricultural credit**.
 
 
 
• **National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID):**
 
 
• Set up in **2021** under the **NaBFID Act, 2021**, it is the newest **All-India Financial Institution**.
 
• It is headquartered in **Mumbai** and functions as a specialized **Development Financial Institution (DFI)** for **long-term infrastructure financing** in India, supporting projects in sectors like energy, transport, and water.
 
 
 
• **MSME Classification (Revised 2020):**
 
 
• **Micro:** Investment up to **Rs. 1 crore** and Turnover up to **Rs. 5 crore**.
 
• **Small:** Investment up to **Rs. 10 crore** and Turnover up to **Rs. 50 crore**.
 
• **Medium:** Investment up to **Rs. 50 crore** and Turnover up to **Rs. 250 crore**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Regulatory Framework:** There are currently **five All-India Financial Institutions (AIFIs)** regulated and supervised by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)**: **SIDBI, NABARD, EXIM Bank, NHB (National Housing Bank), and NaBFID**.
 
• **MUDRA Bank:** The **Micro Units Development and Refinance Agency (MUDRA)** is a subsidiary of **SIDBI**, launched in **2015** to provide loans up to **10 lakh** to non-corporate, non-farm small/micro-enterprises.
 
• **Udyam Registration:** It is the official portal launched by the **Ministry of MSME** for the registration of **MSMEs**, which **SIDBI** uses to identify and provide credit assistance to valid enterprises.
</ul

questions.question: Who presented India’s Third Voluntary National Review (VNR) Report on Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) in July 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **Vice Chairman of NITI Aayog** is the designated authority to present India’s **Voluntary National Review (VNR)** report at the international level. This report is a formal document that tracks the progress made by the country toward achieving the **Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs)**.
 
• In **July 2025**, the **Third VNR** report was presented at the **United Nations High-Level Political Forum (HLPF)** on **Sustainable Development** in **New York**. This forum is the primary global platform for reviewing the **2030 Agenda for Sustainable Development**.
 
• The report outlines India’s journey in localized implementation of the **17 SDGs**, emphasizing the philosophy of **"Viksit Bharat"** (Developed India) and the principle of **"Antyodaya"** (leaving no one behind).
 
• The **VNR** serves as a platform for India to share its best practices, such as the **Digital Public Infrastructure (DPI)**, **clean energy transitions**, and **large-scale social welfare schemes**, with the global community.
 
• The preparation of the report is led by **NITI Aayog**, involving extensive consultations with **State Governments**, **Union Territories**, **Civil Society Organizations (CSOs)**, and the **private sector**. ***Hence, the correct answer is Vice Chairman, NITI Aayog.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India):**
 
 
• Established on **January 1, 2015**, it replaced the erstwhile **Planning Commission**. It acts as the premier policy **think tank** of the **Government of India**.
 
• The **Prime Minister of India** serves as the **Ex-officio Chairperson**, while the **Vice Chairman** is the administrative head appointed by the Prime Minister. As of current tenures, **Shri Suman Bery** serves as the **Vice Chairman**.
 
 
 
• **Evolution of VNRs in India:**
 
 
• India presented its **First VNR** in **2017**, which focused on early implementation strategies.
 
• The **Second VNR** was presented in **2020**, titled **"Decade of Action: Taking SDGs from Global to Local."**
 
• The **Third VNR** continues this trajectory, highlighting the integration of **SDGs** into national development plans and the **Annual Budget**.
 
 
 
• **SDG India Index:**
 
 
• To monitor progress domestically, **NITI Aayog** publishes the **SDG India Index**. It ranks **States and Union Territories** based on their performance across various social, economic, and environmental indicators.
 
• This index fosters a spirit of **competitive federalism**, encouraging states to improve their rankings by achieving specific targets like **Zero Hunger (SDG 2)** and **Gender Equality (SDG 5)**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Key Themes of the Report:** The **Third VNR** specifically highlights the impact of schemes like **Pradhan Mantri Jan Dhan Yojana** for financial inclusion and the **Jal Jeevan Mission** for providing tap water to rural households.
 
• **International Collaboration:** By presenting the **VNR**, India reinforces its commitment to the **Global South**, promoting **South-South Cooperation** and sharing scalable models for poverty eradication and climate resilience.
 
• **Monitoring Framework:** The **Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI)** maintains the **National Indicator Framework (NIF)**, which provides the data backbone for the **VNR** and the **SDG India Index**.
 
• **HLPF Role:** The **High-Level Political Forum** meets annually under the auspices of the **Economic and Social Council (ECOSOC)** to evaluate global progress toward the **2030 targets**.

questions.question: The Income Tax Act, 2025, introduced a new concept to describe assets such as cryptocurrencies and tokenized assets. What is this new concept called?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Virtual Digital Assets**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The term **Virtual Digital Assets (VDA)** was introduced into the **Income Tax Act** to provide a specific legal framework for the taxation of digital assets like **cryptocurrencies** and **tokenized assets**.
 
• As per **Section 2(47A)** of the **Income Tax Act, 1961**, a **Virtual Digital Asset** is defined as any information, code, number, or token generated through cryptographic means or otherwise, providing a digital representation of value.
 
• This definition is broad enough to include **Non-Fungible Tokens (NFTs)** and any other digital asset of a similar nature, ensuring that the digital economy is brought under the tax net.
 
• The **Finance Act, 2022** originally established the taxation regime for these assets, which has been refined in subsequent updates like the **Income Tax Act, 2025**, to ensure transparency and prevent tax evasion.
 
• Income derived from the transfer of any **Virtual Digital Asset** is taxed at a high flat rate of **30%**, regardless of whether the holding period is short-term or long-term.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Tax Deducted at Source (TDS):** To track the transaction trail of **Virtual Digital Assets**, the government introduced **Section 194S**, which mandates a **1% TDS** on payments made for the transfer of such assets if the transaction value exceeds **Rs. 10,000** (or **Rs. 50,000** for specified persons) in a **Financial Year**.
 
• **Treatment of Losses:** One of the most stringent features of the **VDA** tax regime is that losses incurred from the transfer of one **Virtual Digital Asset** cannot be set off against gains from another **VDA** or any other source of income. Furthermore, such losses cannot be carried forward to future **Assessment Years**.
 
• **Cost of Acquisition:** While calculating the taxable income from **VDAs**, no deduction is allowed for any expenditure (such as mining costs or platform fees) other than the actual **cost of acquisition** of the asset.
 
• **Gifts of VDAs:** If a **Virtual Digital Asset** is received as a gift, it is taxable in the hands of the recipient under the head **"Income from Other Sources,"** provided the value exceeds the threshold of **Rs. 50,000**.
 
• **Exclusion of Central Bank Digital Currency (CBDC):** It is important to note that the **Digital Rupee** or **CBDC** issued by the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** is generally not classified as a **Virtual Digital Asset** because it is considered a digital form of legal tender (currency).
</ul

questions.question: Which of the following banks was fined ₹29.6 lakh by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) for violating regulations in June 2025?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Fino Payments Bank**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• In **June 2025**, the **Reserve Bank of India (RBI)** imposed a significant monetary penalty of **₹29.6 lakh** on **Fino Payments Bank Limited**.
 
• The penalty was imposed due to the bank's non-compliance with specific directions issued by the **RBI** regarding **regulatory guidelines** and operational standards expected of **Payments Banks**.
 
• The action was taken under the powers vested in the **RBI** under the provisions of **Section 47A(1)(c)** read with **Section 46(4)(i)** of the **Banking Regulation Act, 1949**.
 
• The **RBI** stated that the penalty was based on deficiencies in **regulatory compliance** and was not intended to pronounce upon the validity of any transaction or agreement entered into by the bank with its **customers**.
 
• A **statutory inspection** and **scrutiny** of the bank revealed that it failed to adhere to the **RBI's** directions on maintaining **customer identification** records and reporting mechanisms.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Fino Payments Bank:**
 
 
• It was incorporated in **2017** and is a subsidiary of **Fino Paytech Limited**.
 
• Headquartered in **Navi Mumbai**, it operates as a **Scheduled Commercial Bank** under the **RBI**.
 
• The bank primarily focuses on **financial inclusion**, offering **savings accounts**, **current accounts**, and **remittance services** to the unbanked and underbanked population.
 
 
 
• **Payments Banks in India:**
 
 
• These are specialized banks introduced by the **RBI** to provide basic **financial services** to **small businesses** and **low-income households**.
 
• They can accept **demand deposits** up to a limit of **₹2 lakh** per individual customer but are **not permitted** to issue **loans** or **credit cards**.
 
• Key players in this sector include **Airtel Payments Bank**, **India Post Payments Bank**, and **Paytm Payments Bank**.
 
 
 
• **Regulatory Oversight:**
 
 
• The **Reserve Bank of India**, established on **April 1, 1935**, serves as the **central bank** and regulatory body for the Indian **banking system**.
 
• It uses **monetary penalties** as a tool to ensure that **financial institutions** maintain **transparency**, **integrity**, and **security** in their operations.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Banking Regulation Act, 1949:** This **Act** provides the legal framework for the supervision of **commercial banks** in India, granting the **RBI** the authority to license banks, regulate shareholding, and impose **penalties** for violations.
 
• **KYC Norms:** **Know Your Customer** guidelines are mandatory for banks to prevent **money laundering** and **financial fraud**. Failure to comply with these often leads to **monetary fines**.
 
• **Compliance Audits:** The **RBI** conducts periodic **audits** and **supervisory reviews** to check the **health** of the banking sector and protect **depositor interests**.
 
• **Financial Inclusion:** The **Nachiket Mor Committee** recommended the creation of **Payments Banks** to reach the **last mile** of the Indian economy.

questions.question: Which company signed an MoU with the Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA) during Aero India 2025, for the development of Flight Control Actuators for the AMCA programme?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Godrej & Boyce Manufacturing Company Limited**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Godrej Aerospace**, a business unit of **Godrej & Boyce**, signed a landmark Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with the **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)**.
 
• The agreement was finalized during **Aero India 2025**, which was the **15th edition** of the biennial air show held in **Bengaluru**.
 
• The primary objective of this collaboration is the indigenous development and manufacturing of **Flight Control Actuators** for India’s **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA)** programme.
 
• This partnership marks a significant milestone in the participation of the **private sector** in critical high-technology defense projects, moving away from reliance on foreign original equipment manufacturers (OEMs).
 
• Under the MoU, **Godrej & Boyce** will focus on the design, development, and testing of complex mechanical and hydraulic systems required for the flight control of **fifth-generation** stealth aircraft.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Advanced Medium Combat Aircraft (AMCA)**:
 
 
• The **AMCA** is an **Indian** programme to develop a **fifth-generation, multirole, stealth fighter**.
 
• It is designed for the **Indian Air Force** to perform roles like air superiority, ground attack, and bombing, featuring **stealth characteristics** and **internal weapons bays**.
 
 
 
• **Aeronautical Development Agency (ADA)**:
 
 
• **ADA** is an autonomous body under the **Department of Defence Research and Development (DRDO)**, established in **1984**.
 
• It is the lead agency for the design and development of combat aircraft in India, including the **Light Combat Aircraft (LCA) Tejas**.
 
 
 
• **Flight Control Actuators**:
 
 
• These are **electro-hydraulic** or **mechanical devices** that move the control surfaces (like ailerons and rudders) of an aircraft in response to inputs.
 
• In high-performance stealth jets like the **AMCA**, these actuators must be highly precise to maintain flight stability and maneuverability at **supersonic speeds**.
 
 
 
• **Aero India 2025**:
 
 
• The event was organized at **Air Force Station Yelahanka, Bengaluru** in **February 2025**.
 
• It served as a major hub for **Atmanirbhar Bharat** initiatives, showcasing domestic manufacturing capabilities in the **aerospace and defense** sectors.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **AMCA project** is a core component of India's long-term defense strategy, aiming to reduce dependence on imported platforms like the **Rafale** or **F-35**.
 
• **Godrej Aerospace** has been a key contributor to India’s space and defense missions for over **three decades**, supplying critical components for **Chandrayaan** and **Mangalyaan**.
 
• The **Cabinet Committee on Security (CCS)** approved the development of the **AMCA** in **March 2024**, with a budget of approximately **Rs. 15,000 crore** for the design and prototype phase.
